issues.description: Type casting of Object.keys(WEIGHTS) to Priority[] is indirect and relies on the reader understanding the relationship between WEIGHTS keys and Priority union type
issues.suggestion: Consider adding a brief inline comment explaining why this cast is safe, e.g., /* Keys are defined as Priority union members */, or extract to a constant with better typing

issues.description: WEIGHTS object could benefit from an explicit type annotation to ensure keys match the Priority type
issues.suggestion: Add explicit type: const WEIGHTS: Record<Priority, number> = { ... } or add JSDoc @type {Record<Priority, number>} to catch mismatches at development time

issues.description: Object.hasOwn() usage is excellent for security (prevents prototype pollution), but this requires Node.js 16.9.0+
issues.suggestion: If supporting older Node versions, document the minimum version requirement in package.json engines field or README, or use Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(WEIGHTS, value) for broader compatibility

codeQuality.summary: Exceptional code quality with modern JavaScript best practices. The module demonstrates excellent security awareness (Object.hasOwn for prototype pollution prevention), immutability (Object.freeze), type safety (comprehensive JSDoc), and functional programming principles (pure functions, no mutations). The code is clean, well-documented, and defensively coded with proper fallbacks. Minor suggestions around type clarity are purely for enhanced maintainability.

untestedPaths.reasoning: Immutability of PRIORITIES array is not explicitly tested. While Object.freeze is used, a test should verify that attempts to modify the array throw errors or fail silently.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: test('PRIORITIES is immutable', () => { assert.throws(() => { PRIORITIES.push('critical'); }); assert.throws(() => { PRIORITIES[0] = 'changed'; }); });

untestedPaths.reasoning: DEFAULT_PRIORITY constant value is used in tests but never explicitly verified to equal 'normal'.
While isPriority is tested against prototype pollution, toPriority should also be explicitly tested to ensure it properly rejects inherited properties and falls back to default.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: test('toPriority rejects prototype properties', () => { assert.equal(toPriority('toString'), DEFAULT_PRIORITY); assert.equal(toPriority('constructor'), DEFAULT_PRIORITY); });

untestedPaths.reasoning: Single-item arrays are a common edge case for sorting functions and should be explicitly tested to ensure no errors occur.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: test('sortByPriority handles a single-item array', () => { const sorted = sortByPriority([{ priority: 'high' }]); assert.deepEqual(sorted, [{ priority: 'high' }]); });

untestedPaths.reasoning: When multiple items have the same priority, sort stability should be verified to ensure predictable ordering.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: test('sortByPriority maintains stable order for same-priority items', () => { const input = [{ id: 1, priority: 'high' }, { id: 2, priority: 'high' }, { id: 3, priority: 'high' }]; const sorted = sortByPriority(input); assert.deepEqual(sorted.map(t => t.id), [1, 2, 3]); });

untestedPaths.reasoning: Arrays are objects and could potentially pass typeof === 'string' if not careful. Should verify arrays containing valid priorities are rejected.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: test('isPriority rejects arrays', () => { assert.equal(isPriority(['low']), false); assert.equal(isPriority([]), false); });

untestedPaths.location: sortByPriority function (line 56-59) - mixed valid and invalid priorities
untestedPaths.reasoning: While missing priorities are tested, explicit testing of todos with junk priority values would strengthen confidence in the robustness of toPriority fallback behavior within sorting.
untestedPaths.suggestedTest: test('sortByPriority handles junk priority values gracefully', () => { const sorted = sortByPriority([{ priority: 'invalid' }, { priority: 'urgent' }, { priority: 42 }]); assert.deepEqual(sorted.map(t => toPriority(t.priority)), ['urgent', 'normal', 'normal']); });

testCoverage.summary: The test coverage for src/utils/priority.js is excellent with 11 well-designed tests covering all exported functions, security concerns (prototype pollution), immutability requirements, and key edge cases including empty arrays and missing properties. The code demonstrates strong testing practices with explicit tests for type safety, fallback behavior, and non-mutation guarantees. Minor gaps exist in: (1) explicit immutability testing for exported constants, (2) prototype pollution testing for toPriority, (3) single-item and stable-sort edge cases for sortByPriority, and (4) array-type rejection in isPriority. These gaps are low-to-medium priority as the existing tests provide strong confidence in correctness. The module is production-ready with 92% estimated coverage.

suggestions.description: The PRIORITIES array is derived from WEIGHTS keys, creating an implicit dependency. This could lead to maintenance issues if priorities need a different iteration order than alphabetical.
suggestions.benefits: Explicit declaration makes the priority order clear and intentional. Runtime validation ensures consistency between PRIORITIES and WEIGHTS, catching configuration errors early.

suggestions.description: Using 'in' operator with a Set for priority checking would provide O(1) lookup performance and clearer intent for membership testing.
suggestions.benefits: Set.has() is semantically clearer for membership testing and provides O(1) lookup. Separates the concern of 'what is valid' (PRIORITY_SET) from 'how priorities are weighted' (WEIGHTS).

recommendations.description: Add explicit tests for prototype pollution resistance in toPriority function and handling of junk priority values in sortByPriority to strengthen security guarantees
Add explicit type annotation to WEIGHTS object to ensure compile-time verification that keys match the Priority type definition
Consider making PRIORITIES declaration explicit rather than derived from Object.keys to improve maintainability and make priority ordering intentional
Consider grouping related test cases using nested test suites for better organization as the test suite grows
